sections.title: The Q2 2026 margin story
sections.subtitle: Gross profit rose 17.5% YoY on revenue up only 7.9%, and operating expenses grew just 1.5%. Gross and operating margins expanded sharply while the net margin fell — that divergence is non-operating, and the charts below are arranged so you can see both halves.

charts.title: Gross vs Operating vs Net Margin
charts.annotation: Q2 2026: gross 70.5%, operating 40.2%, net 23.2%. The gap between the operating and net lines in the last quarter is fair-value declines on equity investments, impairments and a 25.5% effective tax rate (14.7% in Q2 2025) — not operating deterioration.

charts.title: Revenue vs Gross Profit vs Operating Income
Operating Income vs Net Income
charts.annotation: Q2 2026 is the clearest case: operating income ¥12,089.3m but net income only ¥6,980.7m. Read the operating bar for the business and the gap for the investment portfolio and tax rate.

charts.title: Diluted EPS (RMB per ordinary share)
charts.annotation: Per ORDINARY share, not per ADS (1 ADS = 5 ordinary shares). FY2014-FY2019 and most pre-2020 quarters are not sourceable and are left blank rather than plotted as zero.

sections.title: Cash generation, balance sheet & the owner's share
sections.subtitle: Balance-sheet fields are only populated at period ends (about 18 of 59 rows), so those series skip gaps rather than plotting zeros.

charts.title: Free Cash Flow vs Net Income
charts.annotation: FY2025 FCF included an ~¥8.4bn working-capital inflow equal to roughly 116% of that year's revenue increase — the DCF therefore uses a 35% working-capital capture rate rather than carrying the FY2025 margin forward.

charts.title: Cash & Equivalents vs Total Debt
charts.annotation: The CSV cash column is cash and equivalents only. NetEase's full treasury including time deposits and short-term investments is ~¥167.5bn stated; the DCF haircuts it to ¥150.1bn.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: Ordinary shares, ~3,221.6m and gently declining on buybacks (¥20.2bn of buyback cash in the trailing year). Stock-based compensation is only separately disclosed in the last three quarters (Q2 2025 ¥946.4m, Q1 2026 ¥616.2m, Q2 2026 ¥781.7m) — too sparse to chart, so it is described in the help note instead.

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by Segment
segmentRevenue.content:
NetEase reports four revenue lines: games and related value-added services, Youdao, NetEase Cloud Music, and innovative businesses and others.

For NetEase: in Q2 2026 games contributed ¥25,022.8m of ¥30,106.5m total — about 83%. Youdao (¥1,466.9m) and Cloud Music (¥1,977.5m) are separately listed subsidiaries (NYSE: DAO and HKEX: 9899), so NetEase consolidates their revenue while owning less than 100% of their economics.

What to watch:

  • Whether non-gaming segments ever become material — they have hovered near 17% combined for years.
  • Innovative businesses is the most volatile line and has shrunk since FY2023.
  • Segment detail is sparse before FY2023; do not read early gaps as declines to zero.

segmentMix.title: Segment Mix
segmentMix.content:
Each segment as a percentage of total revenue, which shows concentration rather than absolute growth.

For NetEase: this is fundamentally a gaming company and the mix chart says so — games have run above 80% of revenue and the FY2025 gaming share was 81.8%. That concentration is the whole investment case and the whole regulatory risk in one line.

What to watch:

  • Gaming above ~80% means China's NPPA approval regime governs most of the P&L; the December 2023 draft rules cut the stock 28% in one session.
  • A rising Youdao or Cloud Music share would diversify that risk, but neither has moved much.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total net revenues across all four segments, in RMB millions.

For NetEase: revenue grew 7.9% YoY in Q2 2026 to ¥30,106.5m. The longer arc matters more: the 3-year revenue CAGR is only 4.2% while owner free cash flow compounded at 27.5%. That gap is margin expansion, not volume growth, which is why the DCF grows revenue at 7.5% decelerating to 3.0% rather than extrapolating the cash-flow CAGR.

What to watch:

  • New-title contribution — Where Winds Meet and Marvel Rivals are the current swing factors.
  • International revenue (roughly 25-30% of the total) as a hedge against China regulation.
  • Deferred revenue / contract liabilities, which lead reported revenue in a games business.

margins.title: Gross, Operating and Net Margin
margins.content:
Three margins on one axis so the operating story and the reported-earnings story can be compared directly.

For NetEase: Q2 2026 is the quarter to understand. Gross margin reached 70.5% (from 64.7%), driven by gaming gross margin of 76.1% as platform revenue-sharing costs fell. Operating margin hit 40.2% (from ~32%) because opex rose only 1.5%. Yet net margin FELL to 23.2%, because of fair-value declines on equity investments, impairments, and an effective tax rate of 25.5% versus 14.7% a year earlier.

What to watch:

  • Whether the gaming gross-margin gain is durable — it came from one mechanism (channel mix / revenue sharing) and a single-mechanism gain can reverse as fast as it arrived.
  • The tax rate: management treats the step-up as structural (expiring preferential software/HNTE rates), not a timing item.
  • Do not read the net-margin dip as operating weakness; read the operating line for the business.

grossProfit.title: Revenue, Gross Profit and Operating Income
grossProfit.content:
The absolute-currency view of the same margin story: how much of each revenue bar survives cost of revenue and then operating expenses.

For NetEase: in Q2 2026 gross profit rose 17.5% YoY on revenue up 7.9%, and operating income reached ¥12,089.3m. Operating leverage this visible is unusual for a mature gaming company and is the core of the current bull case.

What to watch:

  • The spread between the revenue and gross-profit bars narrowing further would confirm the cost-structure shift.
  • Marketing spend on new title launches is the main lever that can compress operating income quickly.

netIncome.title: Operating Income vs Net Income
netIncome.content:
Operating income is what the business earned from operations; net income adds investment gains and losses, impairments, interest and tax.

For NetEase: these two lines diverged sharply in Q2 2026 — operating income ¥12,089.3m against net income of just ¥6,980.7m, down from ¥10,674.1m in Q1 2026. The fall is entirely below the operating line: equity-investment fair-value declines, impairments and the higher tax rate. A reader who looks only at net income will misread a strong operating quarter as a weak one.

What to watch:

  • NetEase carries a large portfolio of listed and unlisted equity stakes, so net income will keep importing market volatility.
  • Several historical net income values were restated in the latest data rebuild.
  • The DCF values operating cash generation, so it treats the Q2 2026 net income fall as non-operating.

eps.title: Diluted EPS
eps.content:
Diluted earnings per ORDINARY share, in RMB. NetEase's US listing trades as ADSs where 1 ADS = 5 ordinary shares, so an ADS-based EPS would be five times these figures.

For NetEase: EPS compounded at roughly 23.8% over five years (FY2020 ¥3.60 to FY2025 ¥10.48) against a 8.9% revenue CAGR — margin expansion and buybacks doing the work. Quarterly EPS inherits all the net-income volatility described above.

What to watch:

  • FY2014-FY2019 and most pre-2020 quarters are deliberately blank — not sourceable, and shown as gaps rather than zeros.
  • Compare EPS growth against operating income growth to separate buyback effects from operating gains.

fcf.title: Free Cash Flow vs Net Income
fcf.content:
Free cash flow is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. NetEase is asset-light — capex runs under 1% of revenue — so FCF tracks operating cash generation closely.

For NetEase: the DCF works from OWNER free cash flow (¥42,883.9m TTM), which is reported FCF of ¥50,036.6m less stock-based compensation and less net interest income. Interest income is stripped because the cash pile that earns it is added separately in the bridge; leaving both in would count the treasury twice.

What to watch:

  • FY2025 FCF flattered by an ~¥8.4bn working-capital inflow — roughly 116% of that year's revenue increase, and not repeatable.
  • Cash flow lines are only reported at period ends for much of the history, so this series has gaps.
  • Deferred revenue from games funds a structurally negative working-capital cycle.

cashDebt.title: Cash and Debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash and equivalents against total debt at each reported balance-sheet date.

For NetEase: net cash is about 29% of the entire market capitalisation. The company states a treasury of roughly ¥167.5bn including time deposits and short-term investments; the DCF deliberately haircuts this to ¥150.1bn — excluding restricted cash entirely, marking short-term investments at 90%, and applying a 5% repatriation friction for PRC withholding tax on onshore dividends. That ¥17.4bn haircut is roughly 5% of the equity value, so it is worth knowing it was applied.

What to watch:

  • Most of the cash is onshore in RMB; getting it to shareholders costs withholding tax.
  • Buybacks consumed ¥20.2bn of cash in the trailing year.
  • Balance-sheet rows exist only at period ends, so this chart is FY-only.

equity.title: Shareholders' Equity
equity.content:
Book value attributable to shareholders at each reported balance-sheet date.

For NetEase: equity has grown from ¥102.4bn (FY2019) to ¥167.1bn (Q2 2026), but the 5-year equity CAGR of 6.3% is below the revenue CAGR — because NetEase returns a large share of earnings through buybacks and dividends rather than retaining them. The stock trades at about 3.4x book against a 10-year range of 2.9x-4.0x.

What to watch:

  • A large slice of book value is the treasury, not operating assets, which caps how meaningful P/B is here.
  • Equity growth slower than earnings growth is a sign of capital return, not weakness.

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Ordinary shares in issue alongside stock-based compensation expense.

For NetEase: the count is about 3,221.6m ordinary shares and gently declining as buybacks outrun issuance. SBC is only ~2.8% of revenue — very low for a large internet company. The DCF expenses SBC in the cash flows and therefore holds the share count FLAT, rather than both expensing and diluting, which would double-charge the same cost.

What to watch:

  • Because SBC is small, the valuation barely moves on how you treat it — the house/street band is only about 8% of market cap.
  • SBC is only separately disclosed in recent quarters, so that series is short.
  • If this chart ever shows shares in the tens of thousands, the data pipeline has regressed.

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (7.5%, decelerating to 3.0% by Year 10)
dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — reported FCF less SBC less net interest income
dcf.notes: Scenario IVs in HKD. Net cash added in the bridge is the haircut ¥150.1bn, not the stated ¥167.5bn. Sanity check PASSED, with two conditions flagged and disclosed: the price sits at the 71st percentile of its 10-year range (defensible because earnings roughly tripled over that decade, and the 17.6x P/E is below the 22.0x 10-year mean), and the base case embeds modest multiple expansion from 9.9x to 12.8x EV/owner-FCF (still below NetEase's own 12.1x 10-year mean EV/reported-FCF). A reader unwilling to assume any re-rating should look at the WACC 12.5% / terminal growth 1.5% corner of the sensitivity matrix, HK$189.37, which is roughly today's price.
